report.source_text: Abnormal laboratory results included an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) 86, C-reactive protein (CRP) level 13.7, ferritin 835, and d-dimer level 1. Fungal antigen testing revealed negative serum 1-3-β-d glucan, Aspergillus galactomannan, cryptococcal antigens, and urinary Blastomyces and Histoplasma antigens. Bacterial Gram stain and culture of sputum specimen were negative. Acid-fast bacilli (AFB) smears of sequential expectorated sputum specimens were negative. Interferon gamma release assay for Mycobacterium tuberculosis was negative with an appropriate mitogen response. His immunoglobulin levels were normal and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) test was nonreactive. Autoimmune serologies were unrevealing with a negative or normal anti-nuclear antibody test (ANA) panel, anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA), angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) level, and rheumatoid factor.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 26-year-old previously healthy Caucasian male recently enlisted in the US Navy presented to pulmonary clinic with a 3-month history of productive cough, fever, night sweats, myalgias, anorexia, and weight loss. Initial treatment with antibiotics from urgent care resulted in only mild improvement with persistent symptoms. Physical examination was unremarkable with normal vitals, clear lungs, and no palpable lymphadenopathy. Chest X-ray revealed a large right upper lobe cavitary lesion, and CT chest demonstrated a 9×10×14 cm necrotic cavitary lesion with mediastinal adenopathy and compression of the superior vena cava and azygous vein.
